correctness.rationale: For n=4,5,6, A4 acts freely on oriented cells in the sense of no inversions because chosen rook columns are fixed and distinct. Orbit cells in dimension 0..3 have counts (n,binom(n,2),2binom(n,3),2binom(n,4)); a two-orbit parity label gives d2 triangle incidence identical for ± and d3 u^eps=t_jkl^{-eps}-t_ikl^{eps}+t_ijl^{-eps}-t_ijk^{eps}. The one-skeleton is complete and 2-cells fill all triangle loops, so every quotient is simply connected. Independently reconstructed the exact integer parity-orbit boundary matrices for all three widths and computed Smith forms: n=4 d1=1^3,d2=1^3,d3=1^2; n=5 d1=1^4,d2=1^6,d3=1^9; n=6 d1=1^5,d2=1^10,d3=1^24 plus 3, with d2*d3=0. The unit d2 forms and simple connectivity allow a wedge-of-S2 model for the 2-skeleton; pi2=H2 and integral diagonalization of 3-cell attaching maps give Q4=3S2, Q5=5S2+S3, Q6=5S2+Moore(Z/3,2)+5S3. Thus torsion is integral and the claim is only finite widths, no n>=7 extension.
